_comment: DS4 machine tuning profiles. The first entry whose match{chip substring, min_ram_gib} fits this machine is applied: each env var is set as a DEFAULT (setenv overwrite=0), so anything you export yourself still wins. Generate/refresh an entry for your machine with ./tune_profile.sh. Order entries most-specific first.

profiles._comment: M5 Max, MEASURED (81G IQ2XXS, 45s cooldown, alone on box). prefill_by_tokens picks per prefill chunk: nax_half_alu below 7680 tok/chunk, nax_int8 at/above. Measured t/s half-vs-int8: 4096:316/269, 5120:364/309, 6144:395/337, 7168:423/366 (half wins), 8192:378/500 (int8 wins) -> crossover in (7168,8192], boundary=midpoint 7680. Both backends enabled + MPP_FORCE; loader maps ranges to DS4_RESIDENT_MOE_NAX_HALF_MAX_TOKENS=7680.

M3 Ultra: NO NAX (matmul2d is M5-only via ds4_gpu_is_m5_device; nax_half_alu/nax_int8 silently fall back to mul_mm_id), so there is NO per-token GPU-backend split like the M5 entry — the routed GPU path is mul_mm_id at every chunk size, and a nax-style prefill_by_tokens would no-op. M3U's win is DUAL-CLUSTER ANE, gated PER-EXPERT by refs (no per-chunk-token ANE gate exists). refs ~= chunk_tokens/32, so prefill_by_tokens here is informational: it documents the token->refs mapping that ANE_MIN_REFS=64 implies (ANE auto-engages on chunks >~2048 tokens and scales up). To get MEASURED M3U numbers, run tune_profile.sh ON the M3U (this box is M5 Max; M3U cannot be benchmarked here). DS4_FLASH_MOE_ANE_DUAL=1 lights both ANE clusters on the SSD/slot-bank path.
